recipes.name: Easy Grilled Lemon Chicken
ingredients_raw: 4 (6 ounce) skinless, boneless chicken breast halves

steps.text: Rinse chicken breasts and pat dry with paper towels. Stir together the lemon juice, soy sauce, ginger, and black pepper in a bowl; pour into a large, resealable plastic bag. Add the chicken breasts, seal the bag, and massage to evenly coat chicken with lemon juice mixture. Place in refrigerator to marinate at least 20 minutes, or up to 24 hours.
Preheat an outdoor grill for medium-high heat. Lightly oil grill grate, and place about 4 inches from heat source.
Drain and discard marinade from the bag, and place chicken on preheated grill. Cook until chicken is no longer pink and juices run clear, 6 to 8 minutes on each side.

raw_recipe.headline: Easy Grilled Lemon Chicken
raw_recipe.description: Lemon juice, ground ginger, and soy sauce are the base for this easy, made-in-minutes marinade that's a perfect enhancement for grilled, boneless chicken breasts.

review.reviewBody: I compbined two recipes and came up with the best chicken breast recipe ever! I followed the recipe to a tee, except for adding 1/4 tsp. horseradish and 1/4 tsp. garlic powder. I thought the recipe would be too lemony, but it wasn't. I ended up with the most moist, juicy, and tasty chicken breast I've ever made and it was so fat free. Just don't overcook! 6 min. on one side and 8 on the other. Tasted like really good steak!

Didn't have enough lemon juice, so I did 1/2 lemon and 1/2 lime juice. I also added 1tsp of ground ginger to the marinade. Since I don't have a grill, I marinated the chicken for about 2 hours and broiled it for 7-9 minutes on each side (top rack of oven). The chicken is very juicy and flavorful but does have a lemon tang to it. Those not fond of sour foods might not care for this too much. Next time I will be adding some brown sugar to sweeten it up a bit. I will be amking it again!

This was delicious! Juicy and very tasty. I have a problem with dry chicken breasts but this was perfect. I just added fresh chopped garlic to the marinade. Baked it at 400 for 10 minutes per side because here in Maine everything is frozen so we can’t use the grill. Lovely. Thank you for posting

I am gluten intolerant so I substituted Braggs aminos for the soy sauce. I also made a 1/2 recipe rather than a full one since I was only marinating 2 chicken breasts. The chicken was moist and had a nice flavor. However, next time, I will probably use fresh ginger instead of ground ginger to allow the flavor of that spice to come through more clearly.

Super easy start - I actually did 1/3 c each of lemon juice, soy sauce and olive oil. Added minced garlic, rather than ginger, just for my kids. Will try ginger next time. Marinated halved chicken breasts almost 2 hours, then grilled. Great flavor!

I love this marinade as did the whole family! I'm using it for the second time tonight. It's perfect for when I'm not so sure what to make for dinner because I always have these ingredients on hand. I like it just the way it is but tonight I"m going to try some of the other recommendations and add some brown sugar. I also thought about pounding the chicken breasts before marinating them then bread hem with panko and pan fry for some fabulous chicken sandwiches

Tasty, but definitely too salty for me. I used low-sodium soy sauce, and not the full amount at that. I poured in several tablespoons of Mirin, a Japanese sweet rice cooking wine, to help counteract the salt and a little of the tartness of the lemon. (And I love lemon - I made lemony, garlic rice to serve with it.) I made those changes based on tasting the marinade before the chicken went in. Since I wasn't able to cook it the day I started it, it marinated about a day and a half, which blended the flavors quite nicely and also helped reduce the saltiness. I'm also glad I used a bit of fresh ginger, rather than powdered; I almost always use a fresh ingredient or herb when I have it. The saltiness of the original recipe would rate it a 3. To those who would say you can't truthfully rate a recipe unless you make it exactly as written, I say if you taste a recipe going "wrong"as you prepare it, I believe in making slight modifications so you don't have to throw out and waste food. Otherwise, I agree; if you start making major changes before trying it, how can you accurately rate something? It's really a different recipe! Submit it to All Recipes as you prepared it!

I am always trying to find new ways to cook healthy and this one is a keeper. My husband, who is not a fan of plain grilled chicken even loved this dish. This is not plain at all and the marinade is perfectly done. I did make a little extra for basting because I love a lot of juice. My daughter, who is a light eater, asked for 2nds! I personally loved this dish and can eat it every week. I made sure I basted the chicken a little bit more than probably required during cooking and it was so juice and flavorful. I even put a little Dijon mustard on the table for dipping, which my husband loved! Next time I make this dish I am going to make even move marinade and sauté some peppers and onions with it! This is a great dish for the whole family to enjoy!! :)

This has become a go to recipe for my boyfriend and I. We make it at least once a week. I often add some garlic, and whisk in a little olive oil, which helps it not so stick to the grill. Definitely recommend trying this one.
Easy and everyone loved it. I used a tsp of fresh ginger, marinated it for an hour and grilled it on a grill pan on the stove top. Yummy.
we like-y, added some lemon peel & rosemary and 2T honey. yum even baked.

Loved this recipe. Quick and easy marinade with ingredients I always have on hand. I added a touch of garlic powder and marinated for about an hour and grilled over charcoal. Perfectly juicy and delicious. This is one of those recipes that gives major flavor with minimal effort. Thank you!
Added 1/4 c white wine to cut some of the salt. Best and easiest marinade ever. Thank you.
When I say that I'm cooking chicken tonight this is the first dish that my wife requests.
It was good but there was a strong taste of soy sauce so next time maybe just a 1/4 cup of soy sauce
This was very good. I used 2 tsp of minced fresh ginger in place of the ginger powder since I had it. But I've never heard of or had to "rinse and pat dry" chicken breast.
It was simple and fast. My husband enjoyed it. I added a squirt of mustard and some garlic powder. Next time I will add some oil so it is less dry.

The marinade was excellent. I did however make a few changes/additions. I added 1 1/2 TBL brown sugar, couple shakes tabasco, & couple green onions. I only marinated it for about an hour and it still turned out very good and flavorful. Next time I'd like to try an "all night marinade" for this recipe. Thanks Melinda for the recipe!
This is good if you like the flavor of soy sauce. We ended up slathering it with guacamole since none of us cared for the recipe.
Very easy with tons of flavor. Served with sweet potato fries and asparagus. If salt is a problem for you use low sodium soy sauce.
